| [CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) v4 | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." In [TERM-105](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-105.md)'s terms a savings buffer is a replenishable reserve, and its depth sets a deadline: how many bad seasons the household can absorb before ruin. A toy shows the consequence. Savings move +1 or −1 each period, and the household can pay 3 now for 6 later. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. At delay 16 and buffer 8, investing raises expected wealth from 8.15 to 10.30 and lowers survival from 0.846 to 0.835. Covering shocks through the delay lowers the threshold to the outlay alone, which is what graduation programmes' consumption support does. The time pressure here is the planning horizon. Deliberation time and attention are a second sense, left to the scarcity readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
